newsitem.title: USA: Birinyi sees another 10 pct rise in Dow - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Birinyi sees another 10 pct rise in Dow - Barron's.

text.p: Market analyst Laszlo Birinyi, who forecast in February that the Dow Jones Industrial Average would hit 8000 in 1997, sees another 10 percent upside potential in 1997.
But the market analyst also plans to be "easing out" on the way up, Barron's said in its July 21st edition.
"I'm bullish with a lower-case b," Birinyi told the financial weekly.

Birinyi, the president of Birinyi Associates based in Greenwich, Connecticut, relies on an indicator called "money flows" to determine whether there's more buying or selling pressure on the overall market and on individual stocks.

He calculates whether trading volume on balance occurred on downticks or on upticks. Positive money flows indicate that trading is occurring on upticks, a bullish sign, while negative money flows show sellers are dictating prices, Barron's said.
"The money flows are still positive, but not as exuberant as one would expect," Birinyi told Barron's.

Birinyi also applies his money-flow analysis to individual stocks. He says Compaq, Texas Instruments, Bankers Trust, Procter & Gamble, Quaker Oats, Chase Manhattan and Coca-Cola all have solid money flows, and Apple Computer has had a recent surge in money flows.
Stocks with weak money flows now include PepsiCo, Philip Morris, Kimberly-Clark and General Motors.
